reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC9728-2-1.note: Forbidden: a metadata document without resource, or with a value other than the resource identifier. Red: oauth_test.go writeResourceMetadata test fails on got["resource"] != "https://mcp.example/"; oauth_e2e_test.go checks the served document carries resource. Single-polarity marker on the row: the field is emitted unconditionally.

RFC9728-2-2.note: Positive only: oauth_test.go and oauth_e2e_test.go assert authorization_servers is a JSON array holding the configured issuer. No negative tag and no single-polarity marker, so a non-array or non-issuer value is not shown refused by a tagged negative.

RFC9728-3-2.note: TestRFC9728WellKnownInsertedBetweenHostAndPath proves the path clause: 200 at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, 404 at /mcp/.well-known/... and the bare suffix. The query clause ("path and/or query components") has no assertion in the tagged unit: an identifier with a query whose document is served without it, or with the query before the suffix, stays green here. Separately, resourceOriginAndPath (streamable_auth.go) TrimRights every trailing slash of the path, so https://mcp.example/mcp/ is published at .../oauth-protected-resource/mcp, not at the RFC-constructed .../mcp/, and no test catches it.

RFC9728-3.1-2.note: The sentence obliges the party that queries the document ("MUST be queried using an HTTP GET request"). TestRFC9728MetadataQueriedWithGET proves the neighbouring publisher rule: Ze answers GET 200 and refuses POST/PUT with 405. Ze fills no metadata-consumer role (the discovery client was excluded 2026-09-21), so no Ze behaviour issues a query and the tags prove a different obligation.

RFC9728-3.1-3.note: The sentence removes only the terminating slash following the host component when the identifier has a path or query. TestRFC9728TerminatingSlashRemovedBeforeInsertion asserts https://mcp.example/mcp/ maps to .../oauth-protected-resource/mcp and its negative forbids any trailing slash: that is the path's own slash, which the RFC keeps (the path is inserted unchanged). The test pins resourceOriginAndPath's strings.TrimRight(u.EscapedPath(), "/"), which conflates /mcp/ and /mcp. The query case (e.g. https://mcp.example/?x=1) is not asserted.

RFC9728-3.2-3.note: Forbidden: a success status other than 200, a content type other than application/json, a body that is not a JSON object, a member outside Section 2. Red: TestRFC9728ResponseShape fails on w.Code != 200, on Content-Type != application/json, on json.Unmarshal into a map (arrays/scalars refused), and on any member absent from rfc9728Section2Members.

RFC9728-3.3-1.note: TestRFC9728ResourceMatchesInsertedIdentifier proves one identifier: resource https://mcp.example/api at .../oauth-protected-resource/api, and that the audience override is not returned. It does not cover an identifier with a trailing path slash: for https://mcp.example/mcp/ Ze forms the URL from /mcp (TrimRight in resourceOriginAndPath) and returns resource https://mcp.example/mcp/, so the returned value differs from the identifier the URL was formed from, and no tagged assertion goes red.

RFC9728-5.1-1.note: Positive only: oauth_test.go TestOAuth_Authenticate_MissingHeader and oauth_e2e_test.go check the 401 WWW-Authenticate contains resource_metadata="https://mcp.example/ (a prefix, not the full metadata URL). No negative tag and no single-polarity marker; the non-Bearer-scheme permission is not exercised.

RFC9728-6-1.note: Forbidden: normalizing either string. Red: TestRFC9728ResourceIdentityPreserved fails if the published resource is not the exact decomposed e+U+0301 identifier (returned != resource), and fails if the composed spelling %C3%A9 retrieves the document (status != 404).

RFC9728-6-2.note: Forbidden: equality other than code-point to code-point. Red: TestRFC9728ResourceIdentityPreserved serves the exact escaped path+query (decodeMetadata requires 200) and requires 404 for the composed spelling, a different query value and a missing query.

RFC9728-6-3.note: Forbidden: comparing without removing JSON escaping, or removing it more than once. Red: TestRFC9728EscapedAudienceMatchesResource fails if verifyJWT refuses an aud with \u0026 against the & identifier; TestRFC9728EscapeTextIsNotUnescapedTwice fails unless a literal \u0026 aud is refused with errJWTAudienceMismatch.

RFC9728-7.1-2.note: TestRFC9728MCPServingTLSVersions proves the protocol-version clause of BCP195: TLS 1.2/1.3 reach MCP, TLS 1.0/1.1 do not. The rest of the BCP195 guidance (RFC 9325 cipher-suite rules, e.g. no NULL, RC4 or sub-112-bit suites) has no assertion in a tagged unit.
